tldr: The paper introduces tool-augmented scientific reasoning as a new task setting where LLMs learn to retrieve and use domain-specific functions rather than solving problems from scratch, with SCIAGENT achieving over 13% absolute accuracy improvement over comparable open-source LLMs on SCITOOLBENCH.
contributions: Proposed a tool-augmented scientific reasoning task setting that shifts focus from omniscient problem-solving to proficient tool use
Constructed MATH-FUNC, a training corpus of 31,375 samples with 5,981 generalized functions
Developed SCIAGENT, an LLM-based agent that plans, retrieves, and uses domain-specific tools for scientific reasoning
Created SCITOOLBENCH, a benchmark with 856 questions and 2,446 functions spanning five scientific domains (Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, EECS, Finance)
methods: MATH-FUNC was built using an automatic pipeline where GPT-4 generates high-level planning, well-documented functions, and function-augmented solutions from the MATH training set. A cross-retrieval strategy was designed to retrieve generalized functions (rather than ad-hoc ones) by temporarily removing original functions and using a trained dense retriever. SCIAGENT comprises four modules: a planning module (generating high-level profiles), a retrieval module (using the fine-tuned dense retriever), an action module (producing interleaved natural language and Python solutions), and a Python executor. The agent was fine-tuned via imitation learning on a mixed dataset of function-augmented solutions (6,229 samples) and function-free solutions (24,946 samples). SCITOOLBENCH was constructed by curating questions from TheoremQA and SciBench, with positive functions generated by GPT-4 and verified by human annotators, and negative functions automatically derived to reduce shortcuts.
results: SCIAGENT-MISTRAL-7B surpasses other comparable open-source LLMs by 13.4% in absolute accuracy. SCIAGENT-DEEPMATH-7B outperforms ChatGPT by a large margin. All evaluated LLMs show higher proficiency in mathematics, finance, and EECS, but lower performance in physics and chemistry. Ablation studies show: (1) the planning module increases function Recall@3 from 48.3% to 53.2% in physics and from 37.3% to 39.8% in chemistry; (2) removing function-augmented solutions causes 5.9% and 5.3% absolute accuracy drops for 7B and 13B models respectively; (3) removing function-free solutions leads to a 14.4% absolute accuracy decrease; (4) performance significantly declines when the retriever is removed; (5) even with 100% hit ratio, accuracy plateaus at around 40%, showing inherent reasoning difficulty remains.
limitations: Open-source LLMs perform far from satisfactory on scientific reasoning benchmarks without tool augmentation. Performance is lower in physics and chemistry domains compared to math, finance, and EECS, likely due to training data distribution gaps. Even with perfect function retrieval (100% hit ratio), accuracy plateaus at approximately 40%, indicating that scientific reasoning itself remains challenging beyond tool access. Constructing and maintaining domain-specific toolsets is acknowledged as sometimes challenging.
